## Signature Block View (SB)

Args: `@blocks` (SignatureBlockField[]), `@contractValue`, `@contractCurrency`, `@contractType`, optional `@title`, `@compact` (hides the verdict footer for list rows).

Renders the ceremony strip: for each line in signing order — party and role, signer and title, the authority ceiling with a pass/fail mark (or "counterparty signer — authority not ours to check"), status pill with date, provider reference, and any findings against that line in red. Below, one verdict: "Document value $5,880 — all authority checks pass." or "N checks fail — the document cannot be executed until each is cleared." with the reasons.

Every check is `verifyCeremony` from signature-block-field, the same function Request Signature and Execute Contract run — so what the screen shows and what the commands enforce cannot diverge. Render-only: no buttons, no writes; the host app mounts the commands beside it.

Styling: document-grade type on `--font-heading`, no motion, a navy seal rule on top, `container-type: inline-size` so lines stack under 420px. Status hues are data (green signed, red blocked) mixed toward the card's own foreground so the pairs survive a dark theme.

### Example

Mounted on Contract's isolated view; see Contract — Acme Industries MSA 2026 (two lines, both signed, checks pass).

### Consumers

Contract — isolated view (over `signatureBlocks`), and Contract Execution App — Workspace tab, where the four ceremony commands sit beside it. Two consumers, unchanged in both: the strip takes the document's value and type as args and asserts no contract-specific rule of its own.

### Non-goals

No actions — Request / Verify / Execute are commands. No per-block editing. Not a signature capture pad.
